ARENA: A large structure for open-air sports or entertainments.
BALLGAME: A field game played with a ball.
BASELINE: The back line bounding each end of a tennis or handball court.
BATON: A hollow cylinder passed from runner to runner in a relay race.
BENCH: The reserve players on a team.
BIRDIE: In golf, a score of one under par on a hole.
BOBSLED: A large sled for two or four people, raced down an ice track.
BOUNDARY: The edge of a playing field; in cricket, a hit to it scoring four or six.
BOWLING: A game in which balls are rolled at an object or group of objects.
BUTTERFLY: A swimming stroke in which both arms swing over the head together while the legs kick together.
CANOEING: The sport of paddling a canoe.
CATCHER: The baseball player stationed behind home plate who catches pitches.
CHAMPIONSHIP: A competition at which a champion is chosen.
CHESS: A board game for two players who move their 16 pieces according to specific rules.
CLEATS: Shoes with leather or metal projections on the soles.
CLIMBING: The sport of climbing rock faces or climbing walls.
CONTENDER: A competitor with a good chance of winning.
CRICKET: A game played with a ball and bat by two teams of 11 players; teams take turns trying to score runs.
CROSSBAR: Game equipment consisting of a horizontal bar to be jumped or vaulted over.
CURLING: A game played on ice in which heavy stones with handles are slid toward a target.
CYCLING: The sport of riding or racing bicycles.
DARTS: A game in which small pointed missiles are thrown at a dartboard.
DEFENCE: The team that is trying to prevent the other team from scoring.
DEFENDER: A player whose main job is to stop the other team scoring.
DEFENSE: The team that is trying to prevent the other team from scoring.
DIAMOND: A baseball field, especially the infield.
DISQUALIFY: To ban a competitor from a contest for breaking the rules.
DIVING: An athletic competition that involves diving into water.
DRAFT: The yearly selection of new players by professional teams.
DRIBBLE: The propulsion of a ball by repeated taps or kicks.
DRIBBLING: The propulsion of a ball by repeated taps or kicks.
DRIVER: A golf club with a large head, used for long shots from the tee.
ENDURANCE: The ability to keep going through long or hard exercise.
EQUESTRIAN: Of horse riding; a person who rides horses, especially in competition.
EQUIPMENT: The gear needed to play a sport.
EXHIBITION: A game or match played for display rather than in competition.
FENCING: The art or sport of fighting with swords.
FINALS: The final match between the winners of all previous matches in an elimination tournament.
FITNESS: Good physical condition, built by exercise.
FORWARD: A position on a basketball, soccer, or hockey team.
GRIDIRON: The playing field on which football is played.
GUARD: A position on the line of scrimmage.
GYMNASIUM: Athletic facility equipped for sports or physical training.
HANDICAP: An allowance given to make a contest fairer, such as extra strokes in golf.
HIKING: A long walk usually for exercise or pleasure.
HOOP: Horizontal circular metal hoop supporting a net through which players try to throw the basketball.
HOOPS: A game played on a court by two opposing teams of 5 players.
HURDLE: A light movable barrier that competitors must leap over in certain races.
HURDLING: A footrace in which contestants must negotiate a series of hurdles.
HURLING: A traditional Irish game resembling hockey; played by two teams of 15 players each.
JOUSTING: A contest in which two mounted knights charge at each other with lances.
KAYAKING: The sport of paddling a kayak.
KNOCKOUT: A blow that renders the opponent unconscious.
LINEUP: The list of players taking part in a game and their positions.
MANAGER: Someone in charge of training an athlete or a team.
MEDALIST: An athlete who has won a medal.
MEDALLIST: An athlete who has won a medal.
MIDFIELDER: A player in the middle of the field, between defence and attack.
MITT: The handwear used by fielders in playing baseball.
OFFENCE: The team that has the ball and is trying to score.
OFFENSE: The team that has the ball and is trying to score.
ORIENTEERING: A race on foot across country, finding checkpoints with a map and compass.
OVERTHROW: In cricket, a throw that misses the stumps and lets the batters run more.
OVERTIME: Extra time played to decide a game that is tied.
PADDLE: Small wooden bat with a flat surface; used for hitting balls in various games.
PASSER: A ball carrier who tries to gain ground by throwing a forward pass.
PASSING: A play that involves one player throwing the ball to a teammate.
PITCHER: The position on a baseball team of the player who throws the ball for a batter to try to hit.
POLO: A game similar to field hockey but played on horseback using long-handled mallets and a wooden ball.
PROSPECT: A young player expected to succeed.
PUCK: A vulcanized rubber disk 3 inches in diameter that is used instead of a ball in ice hockey.
RACER: A person, animal or vehicle that takes part in races.
RACKET: A sports implement used to strike a ball in various games.
RAFTING: Travelling down a fast-flowing river in an inflatable raft.
RALLY: An unbroken sequence of several successive strokes.
RAPPELLING: Abseiling: descending a rock face or wall on a rope.
REBOUND: The act of securing possession of the rebounding basketball after a missed shot.
RECEIVER: The tennis player who receives the serve.
RECORD: An extreme attainment; the best performance ever attested.
RELAY: A race between teams; each member runs or swims part of the distance.
RELEGATION: Being moved down to a lower division or league.
REPLAY: The immediate rebroadcast of some action that has been recorded on videotape.
RIVAL: The contestant you hope to defeat.
ROOKIE: A first-year player in a professional sport.
ROWING: The act of rowing as a sport.
RUNNER: A person who runs, especially in a race.
RUNNING: The sport or exercise of running.
SAILING: The sport of racing or travelling in sailing boats.
SEASON: The part of the year in which a sport's games are played.
SEEDING: Ranking players in a tournament so the strongest do not meet early.
SERVE: A stroke that puts the ball in play.
SHOOTING: The sport of firing guns at targets.
SHOOTOUT: A tiebreak in which players take turns shooting at goal.
SINGLES: A game, as in tennis, with one player on each side.
SKATING: The sport of gliding on skates.
SKELETON: A winter sport of sliding head first down an ice track on a small sled.
SKIING: A sport in which participants must travel on skis.
SNOWBOARDING: The act of sliding down a snow-covered slope while standing on a snowboard.
SNOWSHOEING: Walking or racing over snow in snowshoes.
SPECTATOR: A person who watches a sporting event.
SPIKE: Sports equipment consisting of a sharp point on the sole of a shoe worn by athletes.
SPRINTING: Running at full speed over a short distance.
SQUASH: A game for two players who hit a small rubber ball against the walls of an enclosed court.
STANCE: The position of a player's feet and body when preparing to play.
STANDINGS: An ordered listing of scores or results showing the relative positions of competitors.
STARTER: A contestant in a team sport who is in the game at the beginning.
STOPPAGE: A break in play, as for an injury.
SUBSTITUTE: An athlete who plays only when a starter on the team is replaced.
SURFING: The sport of riding a surfboard toward the shore on the crest of a wave.
SWEEPER: A defender who plays behind the other defenders.
SWIMMING: The sport of moving through water using the arms and legs.
TACKLE: An attempt to take the ball from an opponent or to bring a ball carrier down.
TACTICS: The planned ways a player or team tries to win.
TAILBACK: In American football, the running back who lines up deepest in the backfield.
TECHNICAL: A foul that can be assessed on a player or a coach or a team for unsportsmanlike conduct.
TOBOGGANING: Riding on a long light sled with low handrails.
TRACKERS: Athletes who compete in track events.
TRIALS: A preliminary competition to determine qualifications.
TROPHY: Something given as a token of victory.
TRYOUT: A test of the suitability of a performer.
TUBING: Riding an inflated tube down a river or snowy slope.
TURNOVER: Losing possession of the ball to the other team.
UPSET: An unexpected win by the weaker competitor.
VARSITY: A school's or university's main sports team.
VAULTING: Leaping over a vaulting horse or with a pole, as in gymnastics and athletics.
VOLLEY: A tennis return made by hitting the ball before it bounces.
WALKOVER: A win given when the opponent fails to turn up; an easy victory.
WHISTLE: A small instrument blown by a referee to stop or start play.
WINDSURFING: Riding a board with a sail across water.
WINGBACK: The position of the offensive back who lines up behind or outside the end.
WINGSPAN: The distance between the fingertips with arms outstretched.
WRESTLING: The sport of hand-to-hand struggle between unarmed contestants who try to throw each other down.
YACHTING: The sport of racing or sailing yachts.
ZONE: An area of a pitch or court; also a defence in which each player guards an area.
